type: type index 92 (named tfbProceduralUVAnimTrack in the section-0 type table): compiled script/behaviour record; header-table entry; blob = [entry, next entry)
structure: Type-92 records are scripts, not entity wrappers; the spawn "owner" is the level-init script

location.offset: all 157 header-table entries of type 92 in the tutorial

meaning: Every one of the 157 type-92 table records references a compiled script (.ai path such as Activate_Jumpad.ai, Chompy_Sprite_, WaterVFX_Remover.ai, LootSystem_Init, InitializeLevel.ai) and script opcodes ("set value||=", "check value", "create variable||with|members", "clone||at|facing||cloned", PRESCRIPT/STARTUP/MACROS/INTERFACE sections). Their blob children (sprites, lists, placements, the spawn tfbPhysicsModel) are the script`s referenced resources and variables. 114/157 have more than five external pointers into their blob: scripts form a web, not self-contained entities. Consequences: (1) the M3 subject cloned so far — the type-92 "spawn owner" — is the level-initialisation script, effectively a singleton; duplicating it re-runs level init and freezes regardless of file layout, which explains why all four registration paths froze; the overwritten target 0x3EDEFC was the LootSystem_Init (STARTUP) script. (2) Entity duplication must target world entities reached through pointers, not table records. The section-0 type name for index 92 is therefore wrong or generic for this game.
